question: Which of the following best describes the key biological difference between Type I and Type II endometrial cancer?

answers.text: Type I is oestrogen-driven, endometrioid histology, lower grade, and generally better prognosis; Type II is oestrogen-independent, includes serous and clear-cell histology, and is high-grade with worse prognosis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Type I arises on the background of unopposed oestrogen exposure (obesity, PCOS, exogenous oestrogens), is typically endometrioid, Grade 1–2, and has ~90% 5-year survival at Stage I. Type II (serous, clear-cell) is oestrogen-independent, associated with p53 mutations, and is aggressive.

answers.text: Type I is associated with p53 mutations and accounts for 80% of all endometrial cancers

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. p53 mutations characterise Type II (serous) endometrial cancer. Type I is driven by oestrogen excess and accounts for approximately 80% of cases, but its molecular hallmark is microsatellite instability and PTEN mutations, not p53.

answers.text: Type II endometrial cancer arises on a background of atypical endometrial hyperplasia and is the more common form

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Atypical endometrial hyperplasia (AEH) is the precursor lesion for Type I (endometrioid) cancer. Type II arises without an AEH precursor and is less common (~20% of cases).

answers.text: Both types are staged by the same FIGO criteria but treated with different chemotherapy regimens

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Both types use the same staging system (FIGO 2023), but the key difference is their biological origin and prognosis, not merely chemotherapy choice.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the Type I/Type II endometrial cancer dichotomy: Type I is oestrogen-driven; Type II is oestrogen-independent, p53-mutated, and includes serous histology.
Correct. Type I = oestrogen-dependent, endometrioid, good prognosis. Type II = oestrogen-independent, serous/clear-cell, aggressive.
